stemBlocks.value: In a class of 80 students, 52 are girls. (a) What percentage are girls? (b) What percentage are boys?
Think first: Every percentage is a fraction of the whole written in hundredths, so decide what the whole is first: here it is the 80 students.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p019-q14 from workbook page 19.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the girls as a fraction of the class.
Multiply by 100 to convert to a percentage.
Convert the boys to a percentage, or subtract from 100%.

strategyBlocks.value: Write the number of girls as a fraction of the total and multiply by 100, then get the boys either by subtracting from 100% or by repeating the process.

whyThisWorks.value: A percentage is a fraction rewritten with denominator 100. Girls and boys make up the whole class, so their fractions add to 1 and their percentages add to 100%. That is why the second answer can be found by subtraction, and why the subtraction also checks the first answer.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing 80 by 52 instead of 52 by 80.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to multiply by 100 and writing 0.65%.

commonErrors.misconception: Not noticing that the two answers must total 100%.

examTip.value: Name the whole before dividing. The quantity following out of, in a class of, or of the is the denominator.
